zh.title: 大梦 · 人生调研
zh.subtitle: 一次关于你的、足够长的问答
zh.intro: 这不是心理测试，也没有分数。它更像一次漫长的、有结构的自我口述史：先把你放回此时此地，再沿时间往回走，经过家庭、性格、爱、工作、欲望和恐惧，最后回到你想留下什么。答案没有对错，只有像不像你。
rules: 先写记得的，不必完整。空白和「想不起来」本身就是信息。
尽量写具体的事，而不是对自己的评价。评价会骗人，场景不会。
任何一题都可以跳过。标注「可跳过」的题目涉及隐私，跳过后不影响档案生成。
所有内容只存在这台电脑上（data/dream.db）。不联网、不上传。
建议分 4–8 次完成，每次 30–60 分钟。情绪被勾起来时，停下来，不必硬撑。
zh.ethics: 数字人是镜子，不是替身。不要用它冒充你做出承诺、签署、转账或操纵他人；涉密与创伤内容默认归入私密层，只有你明确授权时才会进入可对话的档案。

en.title: Dameng · Life Survey
en.subtitle: A life survey, distilled into a digital twin
en.intro: This is not a personality test, and there is no score. It is closer to a long, structured oral history: first it puts you back in the present, then walks backward through family, character, love, work, desire and fear, and finally returns to what you want to leave behind. There are no right answers—only answers that sound like you.
rules: Write what you remember first; it does not need to be complete. Blank spaces and “I can't remember” are information too.
Aim for specific events, not evaluations of yourself. Evaluations lie; scenes do not.
You can skip any question. Questions marked “optional” touch on privacy; skipping them does not keep the archive from being generated.
Everything stays on this computer (data/dream.db). No network, no uploads.
Do it in 4–8 sittings of 30–60 minutes. If something stirs you up, stop; you do not have to push through.
en.ethics: The digital twin is a mirror, not a stand-in. Do not use it to impersonate you in promises, signatures, transfers or manipulation. Private and traumatic material goes into the private layer by default; it enters the conversational archive only with your explicit permission.

ja.title: 大夢 · 人生調査
ja.subtitle: 人生を尋ね、デジタルツインへ蒸留する
ja.intro: これは心理テストではなく、点数もありません。むしろ、長く構造化された自分史の口述です。まず今ここに戻り、時間をさかのぼって家族、性格、愛、仕事、欲望、恐れを通り、最後に「何を残したいか」へ戻ります。正しい答えはありません。あるのは「自分らしいかどうか」だけです。
rules: まず覚えていることを書いてください。完結していなくて構いません。空白や「思い出せない」も情報です。
自分への評価よりも、具体的な出来事を書いてください。評価は嘘をつきますが、場面は嘘をつきません。
どの質問も飛ばせます。「飛ばしてよい」とある質問はプライバシーに関わります。飛ばしてもアーカイブは作れます。
内容はこのパソコン（data/dream.db）にだけ保存されます。ネット接続もアップロードもありません。
4〜8 回、1 回 30〜60 分を目安にしてください。感情が動いたら、そこで止まってかまいません。無理に続ける必要はありません。
ja.ethics: デジタルツインは鏡であり、身代わりではありません。本人として約束する、署名する、送金する、他人を操作するために使わないでください。私的な内容やトラウマはデフォルトで私的レイヤーに入り、あなたが明示的に許可したときだけ会話用アーカイブに入ります。

ko.title: 대몽 · 인생 조사
ko.subtitle: 인생을 묻고, 디지털 트윈으로 증류하다
ko.intro: 이것은 심리 테스트가 아니고 점수도 없습니다. 오히려 길고 구조화된 자기 구술사에 가깝습니다. 먼저 지금 이 자리로 돌아오고, 시간을 거슬러 가족, 성격, 사랑, 일, 욕망, 두려움을 지나 마지막으로 '무엇을 남기고 싶은가'로 돌아옵니다. 맞는 답은 없습니다. '나다운가'만 있을 뿐입니다.
rules: 먼저 기억나는 대로 쓰세요. 완전하지 않아도 됩니다. 빈칸과 '기억나지 않는다'도 정보입니다.
자기 평가보다 구체적인 사건을 쓰세요. 평가는 거짓말을 하지만 장면은 거짓말하지 않습니다.
어떤 질문이든 건너뛸 수 있습니다. '건너뛰어도 됨'이라고 표시된 질문은 사생활과 관련되며, 건너뛰어도 아카이브는 만들어집니다.
모든 내용은 이 컴퓨터(data/dream.db)에만 저장됩니다. 네트워크도 업로드도 없습니다.
4~8번, 한 번에 30~60분을 권합니다. 감정이 올라오면 멈추세요. 억지로 버틸 필요는 없습니다.
ko.ethics: 디지털 트윈은 거울이지 대리인이 아닙니다. 본인으로서 약속하거나 서명하거나 송금하거나 타인을 조종하는 데 쓰지 마세요. 사적인 내용과 트라우마는 기본적으로 사적 레이어에 들어가며, 당신이 명시적으로 허락할 때만 대화용 아카이브에 들어갑니다.

zh.title: 坐标与当下
zh.subtitle: 先把你放回此时此地
zh.why: 数字人最容易犯的错，是只有观点没有生活。这一章先把你的身体、时间、钱和日常放进来——它们决定了你说话的底气和疲惫的来源。

questions.title: 三句话的自我介绍
questions.prompt: 用三句话介绍现在的你。第一句：你是谁（身份、角色）；第二句：你正在做什么（工作、生活重心）；第三句：此刻你最在意、最放不下的是什么。
questions.hint: 不要写成简历。写成你半夜对自己说的话。三句就够，不用展开。
probes: 如果只能留一句，是哪一句？
这三句里，哪一句最不像你？

questions.title: 基本坐标
questions.prompt: 出生年份与地点、现在住在哪、和谁一起住、做什么工作、母语/方言/外语、家庭结构（父母、兄弟姐妹、婚姻、孩子）。
questions.hint: 像填一份只有你自己看的档案，事实清单即可。
probes: 过去十年搬过几次家？哪一次最舍不得？
你现在住的地方，最像你的一个角落是哪里？

questions.title: 一个普通工作日
questions.prompt: 从睁眼到闭眼，一个普通的工作日怎么过？按时间写：起床、手机、吃饭、通勤、工作、独处、睡前。
questions.hint: 越琐碎越好。写你实际做的，不是应该做的。
probes: 哪个时刻最像你自己？
哪个时刻你最想逃？

questions.title: 一个普通周末
questions.prompt: 一个没有安排的周末，你会怎么过？和谁、在哪里、做什么？如果周末被安排了，你心里什么感觉？
questions.hint: 写最近一个真实的周末，而不是理想的周末。
probes: 独处和社交的比例大概是多少？
周末结束时你通常什么心情？

questions.title: 身体这台机器
questions.prompt: 你现在的身体状态：睡眠、精力、运动、疼痛或慢性问题、饮食、体检有没有异常。你和身体的关系怎么样？
questions.hint: 身体是最诚实的传记。写具体数字：几点睡、睡几小时、多久运动一次。
probes: 身体有没有哪个部位，一想到就叹气？
你上一次觉得自己身体很好，是什么时候？

questions.title: 钱的位置
questions.prompt: 你现在的钱：收入来源和大致结构、负债、存款给你的安全感、最近一笔大开销、最后悔的一笔花费。
questions.hint: 不需要精确数字，用区间和比例即可。重点是你对钱的感觉，不是账本。
probes: 你上一次为钱失眠是什么时候？
如果收入突然断了，你能撑多久？

questions.title: 时间的饼图
questions.prompt: 过去一年，你的时间大概花在了哪几件事上？给一个粗略的饼图（百分比），并标出哪一块是你真正想花的。
probes: 哪一块最让你意外？
如果砍掉一块，你砍哪块？

questions.title: 最近一次大笑，最近一次哭
questions.prompt: 最近一次真心大笑是什么时候、因为什么？最近一次哭（或差点哭）是什么时候、因为什么？
questions.hint: 要具体的场景和那句让你笑/哭的话。
probes: 你笑点低还是泪点低？
你会在别人面前哭吗？

questions.title: 如果现在的生活是一部电影
questions.prompt: 片名是什么？第一幕是什么画面？如果给这部电影写一句宣传语，会是什么？
questions.hint: 第一反应最准，不要想太久。
probes: 这部电影是什么类型？
你希望结局是什么样？

questions.title: 最了解你的人会怎么说
questions.prompt: 你身边最了解你的那个人，会怎么描述你现在的状态？用他/她的语气写，不要用你自己的语气。
questions.hint: 想象他/她正坐在对面，跟一个陌生人介绍你。
probes: 他/她最担心你什么？
他/她说的哪一点你会否认？

zh.title: 人生时间线
zh.subtitle: 十个锚点，把你重新走一遍
zh.why: 性格不是凭空长出来的，它是一连串具体事件留下的姿势。这一章用场景而不是结论来重建你的时间线——数字人的「记忆」只能来自这里。

questions.title: 最早的记忆
questions.prompt: 你最早的记忆是什么？大约几岁？画面、气味、声音、光线、谁在场、你当时什么感觉。
questions.hint: 不用确定年龄。哪怕只是一个画面、一种味道，也写下来。
probes: 那个场景里，你最想改变的是什么？
这段记忆你后来跟谁讲过？

questions.title: 童年（约 7–12 岁）
questions.prompt: 那时候家是什么样的？学校呢？最好的朋友是谁？最怕什么？最骄傲的一件事是什么？
questions.hint: 写一个具体的下午或一件事，比概括「童年很幸福」有用得多。
probes: 那时候你觉得自己是什么样的小孩？
有没有一个大人真正看见过你？

questions.title: 一件改变你对自己的看法的事
questions.prompt: 在童年或少年时期，有没有一件事，让你对自己的看法变了？可以是变好，也可以是变坏。
questions.hint: 例如一次比赛、一次被冤枉、一次转学、一次被表扬。
probes: 如果那件事没有发生，你会成为什么样的人？
你现在还相信当时的结论吗？

questions.title: 青春期（约 13–18 岁）
questions.prompt: 身体的变化、叛逆、秘密、第一次喜欢一个人、第一次被否定、和父母的关系——挑你记得最清楚的写。
questions.hint: 不用面面俱到。写那个让你现在想起来还会脸红或心口一紧的片段。
probes: 那时候你最大的秘密是什么？
你反抗过什么？结果呢？

questions.title: 第一次重大选择
questions.prompt: 高考、选专业、去哪个城市、第一份工作——你第一次真正意义上的重大选择是什么？你选了什么，谁做的决定，代价是什么？
questions.hint: 重点不是结果好坏，而是当时你怎么想的、谁影响了你的决定。
probes: 如果重来，你会选另一个吗？
这个选择现在还在影响你什么？

questions.title: 第一次离开家（约 18–22 岁）
questions.prompt: 第一次长期离开家是什么时候？去了哪里？遇见了谁？学会了什么？失去了什么？
questions.hint: 写一件只有离开家才会发生的事。
probes: 你什么时候开始想家？
你第一次觉得自己「长大了」是什么时刻？

questions.title: 第一次真正独立，第一次重大失败（约 22–28 岁）
questions.prompt: 第一次靠自己生活是什么样？第一份工作教会了你什么？第一次重大失败是什么，你怎么缓过来的？
questions.hint: 可以写两份工作、一次分手、一次考试、一次创业。写具体。
probes: 那次失败改变了你什么？
谁在那段时间接住了你？

questions.title: 28 岁到现在：三次转折
questions.prompt: 从 28 岁到现在，你人生中最重要的三次转折是什么？（换城市、换工作、结婚/离婚、生病、亲人去世、开始做一件事……）每次你是怎么决定的？
questions.hint: 按时间顺序写。写不动就只写标题，之后再补细节。
probes: 哪一次是你主动选的？哪一次是被推着走的？
这三次转折有共同点吗？

questions.title: 最低谷
questions.prompt: 到目前为止的人生最低谷是什么时候？发生了什么？你每天怎么过？谁在？你怎么活过来的？
questions.hint: 可以模糊细节。如果现在写会难受，先写一句「有一段时间……」也可以。
probes: 那时候你最需要听到什么话？
你有没有想过放弃？是什么留住了你？

questions.title: 最高光
questions.prompt: 人生最高光的时刻是什么？发生了什么？你当时什么感觉？之后为什么没有延续？
questions.hint: 高光不一定是世俗成功，也可能是某个下午你觉得自己完整。
probes: 那一刻你最想告诉谁？
你现在还会想起它吗？

questions.title: 人生曲线：五个点
questions.prompt: 如果把人生画成一条曲线（横轴年龄，纵轴状态），请写出五个关键点：年龄 + 状态 + 一个词命名。
questions.hint: 例如：6 岁，高，外婆家；16 岁，低，被否定；24 岁，高，第一份工作……
probes: 曲线现在的趋势是什么？
你希望下一个点在哪里？

questions.title: 平行人生
questions.prompt: 有没有一个「差点成为的你」？当时差在哪一步？你现在还会想起那个人吗？
questions.hint: 可以是另一个专业、另一座城市、另一段关系、另一个职业。
probes: 你后悔吗？
那个版本的你，有什么是你现在缺的？

zh.title: 家庭与依恋
zh.subtitle: 你最早学会的爱的方式
zh.why: 一个人怎么处理冲突、怎么表达需要、怎么面对分离，大多在童年餐桌上就写好了初稿。这一章不是审判父母，而是看清你继承了什么、又拒绝了什么。

questions.title: 父亲
questions.prompt: 你的父亲是一个什么样的人？用三个词形容他。他做过最影响你的一件事是什么？你像他吗？
questions.hint: 写具体的画面：他的口头禅、他的手、他生气时的样子。
probes: 你最想从他那里得到什么？
你最不想成为他的哪一点？

questions.title: 母亲
questions.prompt: 你的母亲是一个什么样的人？用三个词形容她。她做过最影响你的一件事是什么？你像她吗？
questions.hint: 同样写具体画面，而不是「她很辛苦」这类总结。
probes: 你最想从她那里得到什么？
你最不想成为她的哪一点？

questions.title: 家规、禁忌与不能说的话
questions.prompt: 你家里有哪些明规则和潜规则？什么话题不能提？什么情绪不被允许？犯了什么错会被惩罚？
questions.hint: 例如：不许哭、不许顶嘴、成绩不好就冷战、钱的事小孩别问。
probes: 你违反过哪一条？后果是什么？
这些规则现在还在你身上吗？

questions.title: 哭了、考砸了、闯祸了
questions.prompt: 小时候你哭了、考砸了、闯祸了，家里通常怎么处理？请各举一个真实例子。
questions.hint: 重点写大人的第一反应，和你的第一反应。
probes: 你那时候希望他们怎么做？
现在你难过时，会怎么对待自己？

questions.title: 继承与拒绝继承
questions.prompt: 你从家里继承了什么？（习惯、信念、恐惧、身体、说话方式）你明确拒绝继承什么？
questions.hint: 各写三条。拒绝继承的那部分，你现在做到了吗？
probes: 有没有哪一刻你发现自己「越来越像我妈/我爸」？
你为拒绝继承付出过什么代价？

questions.title: 现在和父母的关系
questions.prompt: 你们现在多久联系一次？聊什么、不聊什么？你为他们做过什么？他们为你做过什么？
questions.hint: 写最近一次通话的内容和气氛。
probes: 你有没有话想对他们说但没说？
他们现在最担心你什么？

questions.title: 家里不能说的秘密
questions.prompt: 你家里有没有一件「大家都知道但从来不提」的事？或者一个秘密？
questions.hint: 可跳过。可以用模糊的方式写，比如「关于舅舅的一段时间」。
probes: 这件事怎么影响了你？
你会把它带进自己的家庭吗？

questions.title: 不想重复的养育方式
questions.prompt: 如果你有孩子（或将来有），你绝对不想重复的养育方式是什么？你希望自己做到什么？
questions.hint: 写具体行为，不写口号。
probes: 你觉得自己能做到吗？
你最怕自己脱口而出的那句话是什么？

questions.title: 父母是普通人的那一刻
questions.prompt: 你什么时候第一次意识到父母只是普通人、会犯错、也会死？当时发生了什么？
questions.hint: 可能是一次生病、一次争吵、一次你发现他们也不懂。
probes: 那之后你对他们的态度变了吗？
你现在怎么理解他们？

questions.title: 家是什么
questions.prompt: 「家」对你来说是什么？如果家是一个人，他/她会是谁、什么性格、会对你说什么？
questions.hint: 用比喻，别用定义。
probes: 你现在有「家」的感觉吗？在哪里？
你理想中的家是什么样？

zh.title: 性格的行为证据
zh.subtitle: 别形容自己，讲发生了什么
zh.why: 「我比较内向」几乎不能用来建模；「聚会到第 90 分钟我会去阳台待十分钟」可以。这一章用场景和反例来定位你的性格，而不是贴标签。

questions.title: 社交电量
questions.prompt: 和一群人待在一起，你的电量通常怎么变化？
questions.hint: 想一个具体的群体：同事、朋友、家人。不同群体可以不同，先写平均值。
probes: 哪种人最耗你的电？
哪种人让你不用表演？
questions.left: 独处三小时才回血
questions.right: 人越多越聊越有电

questions.title: 秩序感
questions.prompt: 你的生活有多需要计划和秩序？
questions.hint: 看你的桌面、行李、待办、旅行方式，不要看你的理想。
probes: 哪里必须整齐？哪里可以乱？
计划被打乱时你第一反应是什么？
questions.left: 随性，计划就是用来打破的
questions.right: 一切要提前排好才安心

questions.title: 情绪波动
questions.prompt: 你的情绪起伏有多大？
questions.hint: 回想最近一个月：你有几天情绪明显偏离平常？
probes: 什么最容易把你推上去？什么最容易把你拉下来？
别人能看出来吗？
questions.left: 像湖面，很少有浪
questions.right: 像海，涨落很明显

questions.title: 开放度
questions.prompt: 面对新事物（新餐厅、新观点、新地方、新工具），你通常什么态度？
questions.hint: 分开想：吃、玩、工作方法、价值观。你可能只在某些方面开放。
probes: 你最近主动尝试的一件新事是什么？
有什么新东西你坚决不碰？
questions.left: 熟悉的就好，别折腾
questions.right: 新鲜的最重要，先试了再说

questions.title: 锋利度
questions.prompt: 当你要说一句可能让人不舒服的真话时，你通常怎么处理？
questions.hint: 想最近一次你指出别人问题，或者忍住没说的场景。
probes: 你伤过人吗？后来怎么处理的？
你希望别人对你说真话吗？
questions.left: 先顾和气，能不说就不说
questions.right: 先把话说直，再管感受

questions.title: 聚会进行到第 90 分钟
questions.prompt: 一场聚会进行到第 90 分钟，你在哪里？在做什么？心里在想什么？
questions.hint: 写你的身体动作：看手机、去阳台、洗碗、找人一对一聊。
probes: 你什么时候会提前走？怎么开口？
你在聚会上通常和谁待最久？

questions.title: 答应别人的事，答应自己的事
questions.prompt: 你答应别人的事，和你答应自己的事，哪个更容易做到？各举一个最近的例子。
questions.hint: 比如「帮同事改方案」vs「给自己写东西」。
probes: 你对自己失约时，会怎么解释？
别人失约时，你会怎么想？

questions.title: 桌面、房间、手机主屏
questions.prompt: 你现在的桌面、房间、手机主屏分别是什么样？秩序在哪里，混乱在哪里？
questions.hint: 可以拍张照，然后用文字描述。不用整理后再写。
probes: 你的混乱有规律吗？
别人动你的东西你会怎样？

questions.title: 最近一次真的生气
questions.prompt: 最近一次你真正生气（或非常烦躁）是什么时候？触发点是什么？你做了什么？事后怎么收场？
questions.hint: 写你身体的第一反应：脸热、手抖、想摔东西、想消失。
probes: 你生气的模式是什么：爆发、冷战、讲道理、还是记账？
你希望对方当时怎么做？

questions.title: 最近一次真的难过
questions.prompt: 最近一次你真正难过是什么时候？你怎么处理？找谁，还是自己扛？
questions.hint: 如果哭不出来，写那种「堵着」的感觉也可以。
probes: 你最不希望谁看见你难过？
什么能真的安慰到你？

questions.title: 独处
questions.prompt: 你需要独处吗？多久？没有独处你会变成什么样？独处时你通常做什么？
questions.hint: 区分「一个人待着」和「真正属于自己的时间」。
probes: 你一个人时最常想什么？
你会害怕独处吗？

questions.title: 被夸和被批评
questions.prompt: 别人夸你时你什么反应？别人批评你时呢？各举最近一个真实例子。
questions.hint: 写你嘴上说的和心里想的，可能不一样。
probes: 哪句夸奖你记了很久？
哪句批评到现在还扎你？

questions.title: 最不能忍受的
questions.prompt: 你最不能忍受别人的什么？你自己身上有这个问题吗？
questions.hint: 写三个。第三个通常最难承认。
probes: 遇到这种人你会怎么做？
有没有人说过你「就是这样的人」？

questions.title: 三个圈子里的你
questions.prompt: 如果让三个不同圈子的人（比如家人、同事、老朋友）各用一句话评价你，他们会怎么说？哪一句最准？
questions.hint: 写他们的原话，不要替他们润色。
probes: 哪个圈子里的你最放松？
他们说的加起来，像你吗？

zh.title: 价值与信念
zh.subtitle: 你在为什么付账
zh.why: 价值观不是问卷里选的词，而是你在冲突、代价和取舍里实际保护的东西。这一章要找出你的底线、排序，以及你愿意为之付出什么。

questions.title: 三条底线
questions.prompt: 你绝对不能做的事是什么？列三件，并说为什么。
questions.hint: 不要写「杀人放火」这种所有人都不能做的。写属于你的，比如「不背后说朋友坏话」「不为了钱写违心的东西」。
probes: 有没有人越过你的底线？你怎么处理的？
你为守住底线付出过代价吗？

questions.title: 成功的人生
questions.prompt: 你认为「成功的人生」是什么样？你现在离它多远？
questions.hint: 先写社会标准答案，再写你自己的答案。两个可能不一样。
probes: 你父母认为的成功是什么？你同意吗？
你害怕自己到死都没成功吗？

questions.title: 钱对你意味着什么
questions.prompt: 钱对你意味着什么？多少钱算「够了」？你愿意为钱做什么，不做什么？
questions.hint: 写一个具体数字，以及这个数字背后的生活画面。
probes: 你没钱时最怕什么？
你见过钱改变一个人吗？

questions.title: 排序与牺牲
questions.prompt: 自由、安全、成就、关系、意义——请排序。并说最近一次你为了其中一个牺牲另一个是什么时候。
questions.hint: 先凭直觉排，再看你最近的实际选择是否一致。
probes: 你的排序和你父母/伴侣的排序冲突吗？
如果只能保一个，你保哪个？

questions.title: 你信什么
questions.prompt: 你信什么？（宗教、哲学、科学、命运、因果、运气、努力）你怎么解释坏事发生在好人身上？
questions.hint: 没有信仰也可以写「我不信什么」。
probes: 你祈祷过吗？什么时候？
你有没有过「这是命中注定」的瞬间？

questions.title: 最强烈的立场
questions.prompt: 在政治或社会议题上，你最强烈的立场是什么？你愿意为它付出什么代价？
questions.hint: 可跳过。写你真实的想法，不需要政治正确。
probes: 你身边有人持相反立场吗？你们怎么相处？
你有没有因为立场失去过什么？

questions.title: 尊重与鄙视
questions.prompt: 你尊重什么样的人？鄙视什么样的人？你自己更接近哪一边？
questions.hint: 各写三种人，再写一个具体的人名或形象。
probes: 你尊重的人有什么共同点？
你有没有做过自己鄙视的事？

questions.title: 最近改变的一个信念
questions.prompt: 有没有一个你曾经坚信、最近改变了的看法？是什么让你改变的？
questions.hint: 工作、感情、金钱、人性、自己，都可以。
probes: 改变的过程痛苦吗？
你现在还确定的事是什么？

questions.title: 最后悔的一件事
questions.prompt: 你做过的最不道德、或最后悔的一件事是什么？（可以模糊细节）你后来怎么面对它？
questions.hint: 可跳过。写你愿意写的那部分。
probes: 你道歉了吗？
你原谅自己了吗？

questions.title: 三条人生规则
questions.prompt: 如果只能教给后辈三条人生规则，你会说什么？每条用一句话。
questions.hint: 写你真正做到的那三条，不是你希望自己做到的。
probes: 哪一条你花了很久才学会？
哪一条你现在也做不到？

zh.title: 爱与亲密
zh.subtitle: 你怎样靠近，又怎样退开
zh.why: 亲密关系是性格最藏不住的地方：你怎么表达需要、怎么处理冲突、什么时候逃跑。这一章决定数字人在情感场景里像不像你。

questions.title: 恋爱史
questions.prompt: 你的恋爱史：几段重要的关系？每段怎么开始、怎么结束、你学到了什么？
questions.hint: 不需要细节八卦。写模式：你总是被什么人吸引，又总是在哪里卡住。
probes: 有没有一段你至今没走出来？
你在关系里最容易犯的错是什么？

questions.title: 怎么知道自己爱上了
questions.prompt: 你怎么知道「我爱上了一个人」？身体和脑子分别有什么信号？
questions.hint: 写具体信号：想分享、反复看手机、身体放松、开始害怕。
probes: 你会先表白吗？
你爱一个人时会变成什么样？

questions.title: 你需要什么样的爱
questions.prompt: 你在关系里最需要什么？最怕发生什么？
questions.hint: 需要：陪伴、空间、肯定、稳定、激情、被理解……最怕：被抛弃、被控制、被看穿、失去自己……
probes: 你有没有因为需要太多而羞愧？
你得到过你想要的爱吗？

questions.title: 冲突时的你
questions.prompt: 和伴侣或密友发生冲突时，你是什么样？（追问、逃跑、冷战、爆发、讲道理、妥协）举最近一次。
questions.hint: 写第一分钟和第三天分别发生了什么。
probes: 你怎么和好？谁先低头？
你最受不了对方在冲突里做什么？

questions.title: 怎么表达爱，怎么表达不满
questions.prompt: 你怎么表达爱？对方能收到吗？你怎么表达不满？
questions.hint: 写你的「爱的语言」：做事、送东西、身体接触、陪伴、说话。
probes: 你最常被误解的表达是什么？
你希望对方怎么对你表达？

questions.title: 嫉妒
questions.prompt: 你会嫉妒吗？什么会触发？你怎么处理？
questions.hint: 写最近一次，包括你说了什么、没说什么。
probes: 你会查手机吗？
嫉妒时你更想控制还是想逃？

questions.title: 亲密关系里的隐瞒
questions.prompt: 在亲密关系里，你最大的隐瞒或谎言是什么？（可以只写类型，不写细节）
questions.hint: 可跳过。包括「没说出口的感受」也算。
probes: 你为什么不说？
如果对方知道了会怎样？

questions.title: 忠诚、边界与其他
questions.prompt: 你怎么看忠诚、边界、开放式关系、异地、年龄差？
questions.hint: 写你的真实看法，不用正确。
probes: 你的边界在哪里？
你越过别人的边界吗？

questions.title: 现在的关系状态
questions.prompt: 你现在的关系状态：满意的地方、想改变的地方、不敢说的地方。
questions.hint: 单身也可以写你和自己、和家人、和朋友的关系。
probes: 你最近一次感到亲密是什么时候？
你在等什么？

questions.title: 如果孤独终老
questions.prompt: 如果最后是一个人生活，你会怎么过？你最怕的是什么？
questions.hint: 写画面：住哪、每天做什么、和谁来往。
probes: 你一个人也能过得好吗？
你最怕的是孤独，还是别人的眼光？

zh.title: 工作、野心与金钱
zh.subtitle: 你在世界上想留下什么形状
zh.why: 工作不只是收入，它是你和现实交手的方式。这一章记录你的能力、野心、失败模式，以及你谈起工作时真正的语气。

questions.title: 职业路径
questions.prompt: 你的职业路径：每一份工作/项目，为什么去、为什么走、带走了什么？
questions.hint: 按时间列。写你辞职那天真正的原因。
probes: 哪一段最像你？
你最后悔的一次职业选择是什么？

questions.title: 最擅长与最讨厌
questions.prompt: 你最擅长的事是什么（别人常找你帮忙的）？最不擅长、最讨厌的是什么？
questions.hint: 写具体能力，不写职位。比如「把混乱的需求翻译成流程」而不是「产品经理」。
probes: 你的擅长是怎么练出来的？
你有没有被夸过但自己并不认同的能力？

questions.title: 野心
questions.prompt: 你的野心有多大？你愿意为它牺牲什么？你偷偷想成为谁？
questions.hint: 写那个你不太敢说出口的版本。
probes: 你害怕成功吗？
如果一辈子只是普通，你能接受吗？

questions.title: 面对权威
questions.prompt: 你如何面对老板、客户、权威？举一次你反抗，或一次你妥协。
questions.hint: 写你嘴上说的和心里想的。
probes: 你怕权威吗？
你成为权威后会变成什么样？

questions.title: 面对失败
questions.prompt: 你经历过最大的职业失败是什么？你的第一反应、恢复过程、现在怎么看？
questions.hint: 写你当时对别人怎么解释。
probes: 你从失败里学到的东西，真的用上了吗？
你还会再试一次吗？

questions.title: 卷、躺平与边界
questions.prompt: 你卷吗？你装吗？你怎么看「躺平」？工作和生活的边界在哪里？
questions.hint: 写你实际的作息，不是你的态度。
probes: 你下班后还会想工作吗？
你请假会愧疚吗？

questions.title: 最得意的作品
questions.prompt: 你做过的、最得意的作品或项目是什么？为什么是它？
questions.hint: 可以是工作，也可以是私人项目、一篇文章、一顿饭。
probes: 它现在还在吗？
别人怎么评价它？

questions.title: 如果明天财务自由
questions.prompt: 如果明天财务自由，你会做什么？还会工作吗？会怎么安排一天？
questions.hint: 写第一周，再写第一年。
probes: 你现在的工作里，哪部分是钱买不到的？
你会离开谁？

questions.title: 金钱习惯
questions.prompt: 你的金钱习惯：记账、投资、借贷、AA、请客、和伴侣的钱怎么管？
questions.hint: 写你实际做的，包括让你羞愧的那部分。
probes: 你父母怎么花钱？你像谁？
你买过最值的东西是什么？

questions.title: 职业上最大的恐惧
questions.prompt: 职业上你最大的恐惧是什么？（被淘汰、被看穿、无意义、不如同龄人、没有作品……）
questions.hint: 写那个让你半夜醒来的念头。
probes: 这个恐惧从什么时候开始？
它保护了你什么？

zh.title: 欲望、恐惧与阴影
zh.subtitle: 你不会在饭桌上说的那些
zh.why: 一个只由光明面组成的数字人会像宣传片。真正让人「像」的，是那些不好意思承认的欲望、羞耻和自我破坏。这一章所有题目都可以跳过，也可以只写你愿意写的部分。

questions.title: 最想要但不敢承认的
questions.prompt: 你最想要、但不太敢承认的东西是什么？（被看见、被爱、赢过某人、不用努力、被照顾、报复……）
questions.hint: 写第一反应。这里没有道德评分。
probes: 如果得到了，你会怎样？
你为它做过什么？

questions.title: 最怕别人发现
questions.prompt: 你最怕别人发现你什么？
questions.hint: 写那个「如果被看穿就完了」的点。
probes: 有没有人发现过？
你用什么遮住它？

questions.title: 嫉妒
questions.prompt: 你最近一次嫉妒谁？嫉妒什么？你做了什么？
questions.hint: 嫉妒往往指向你真正想要的东西。
probes: 你承认过自己嫉妒吗？
嫉妒之后你更想努力还是更想毁掉？

questions.title: 羞耻
questions.prompt: 你的羞耻感来自哪里？最羞耻的一段记忆是什么？（可以模糊）
questions.hint: 可跳过。写你身体记得的那个瞬间。
probes: 谁让你感到羞耻？
你现在还会因为什么脸红？

questions.title: 上瘾与失控
questions.prompt: 你有没有上瘾或失控的事？（手机、游戏、酒、购物、工作、关系、性、食物、情绪）
questions.hint: 可跳过。写你试图控制它的方式。
probes: 它帮你逃避什么？
你戒过吗？

questions.title: 自我破坏
questions.prompt: 你会不会在关键时刻把自己搞砸？通常是什么方式？
questions.hint: 例如拖延到最后一刻、突然消失、说伤人的话、故意不睡觉。
probes: 那一刻你在保护什么？
事后你怎么解释？

questions.title: 最黑暗的念头
questions.prompt: 你有过最黑暗的念头是什么？（伤害自己、消失、报复、希望某人消失……）你怎么处理它？
questions.hint: 可跳过。如果此刻正处于危险中，请先联系你信任的人或当地心理援助热线；这道题不急着答。
probes: 这个念头什么时候最强？
什么让它退下去？

questions.title: 最大的谎
questions.prompt: 你撒过最大的谎是什么？对谁？为什么？
questions.hint: 可跳过。也可以写「我对自己撒的谎」。
probes: 这个谎还在继续吗？
你后悔吗？

questions.title: 另一个自己
questions.prompt: 有没有一个「另一个你」——只在深夜、网络、陌生人面前、喝醉后出现？他/她是什么样？
questions.hint: 写那个版本和日常版本的差别。
probes: 你喜欢那个版本吗？
哪个更真实？

questions.title: 如果没有人会知道
questions.prompt: 如果做任何事都不会有人知道、也不用承担后果，你会做什么不一样的事？
questions.hint: 可跳过。写第一反应。
probes: 这说明你平时压抑了什么？
有没有一件小事你现在就可以做？

zh.title: 日常、身体与审美
zh.subtitle: 你身上的小动作和小癖好
zh.why: 「像不像」常常败在细节：你用什么标点、几点洗澡、走路会不会踩线。这一章收集那些看起来没用、却最像你的东西。

questions.title: 你的手机
questions.prompt: 手机主屏长什么样？最常用的五个 App 是什么？屏幕使用时间多少？睡前最后一件事是什么？
questions.hint: 可以直接照实写，包括让你不好意思的那个 App。
probes: 你起床后第一件事是什么？
你试过戒手机吗？

questions.title: 身体习惯
questions.prompt: 睡姿、起床第一件事、咖啡/茶/烟/酒、运动、洗澡时间、每天的固定小动作。
questions.hint: 写你身体的固定程序，像说明书。
probes: 哪个习惯你最想改？
哪个习惯你绝对不会改？

questions.title: 审美
questions.prompt: 你的穿衣风格、家里最像你的物件、最喜欢的颜色/材质/气味。
questions.hint: 写你实际拥有的，不是你想拥有的。
probes: 你买过最「就是你」的东西是什么？
你讨厌什么样的审美？

questions.title: 音乐
questions.prompt: 最近循环的三首歌、一首会让你哭的歌、一首代表你的歌。
questions.hint: 写歌名和歌手，能写一句感受更好。
probes: 你什么时候最需要音乐？
你唱歌吗？

questions.title: 影响你的作品
questions.prompt: 电影、书、游戏、剧——挑三部影响过你的作品，为什么是它们？
questions.hint: 不用选「高级」的，选你真的记得的。
probes: 你最近一次被一部作品击中是什么时候？
你会反复看同一部吗？

questions.title: 你的幽默感
questions.prompt: 什么会让你笑？讲一个你最近觉得好笑的事或段子。你平时怎么开玩笑？
questions.hint: 直接写你当时说的话，不要解释笑点。
probes: 你的幽默偏哪种：冷、损、自嘲、荒诞、谐音？
你会拿谁开玩笑？

questions.title: 语言习惯
questions.prompt: 你的口头禅、打字风格、爱用的表情/标点、语音还是文字、中英夹杂吗？举三句你常说的话。
questions.hint: 打开聊天记录找三句原话，比回忆准。
probes: 你生气时打字会变吗？
你会用「哈」还是「哈哈哈」？

questions.title: 放松、奖励与惩罚
questions.prompt: 你如何放松？如何奖励自己？如何惩罚自己？
questions.hint: 惩罚可能是「不许休息」「暴食」「熬夜」。
probes: 你上一次真正放松是什么时候？
你觉得你配休息吗？

questions.title: 收藏、执念与小癖好
questions.prompt: 你有没有收藏的东西、奇怪的执念、小癖好？（收集杯子、必须摆正、走路不踩线、半夜整理文件夹……）
questions.hint: 越没用越好。
probes: 这些癖好从什么时候开始？
别人知道吗？

questions.title: 最属于自己的 15 分钟
questions.prompt: 一天中，哪 15 分钟最属于你自己？你在做什么？
questions.hint: 写具体时间和地点。
probes: 这 15 分钟被打断你会怎样？
你需要更多这样的时间吗？

zh.title: 决策与思维
zh.subtitle: 你怎么选，怎么后悔
zh.why: 数字人如果不能替你做判断，就只是个聊天玩具。这一章提取你的决策算法：信息、直觉、风险、拖延和后悔的方式。

questions.title: 重大决定的流程
questions.prompt: 你做重大决定时，通常怎么走？（收集信息、问人、凭直觉、拖延、列清单）举最近一个真实决定。
questions.hint: 写从起念到拍板的完整过程，包括你失眠的那晚。
probes: 你最后通常听谁的？
有没有决定做完就后悔的？

questions.title: 最后悔的决定
questions.prompt: 你最后悔的决定是什么？如果重来会怎么选？
questions.hint: 写那个你偶尔还会在洗澡时想起的决定。
probes: 你从里面学到了什么？
你真的会选另一条吗？

questions.title: 风险偏好
questions.prompt: 你是保守还是冒险？在钱、事业、感情上分别如何？举一个你冒险的例子。
questions.hint: 三个领域可能完全不同，分开写。
probes: 你冒过最大的险是什么？
你输得起吗？

questions.title: 直觉
questions.prompt: 你相信直觉吗？有没有一次直觉救了你，或害了你？
questions.hint: 写身体的感觉：胃紧、后背发凉、莫名安心。
probes: 你通常忽略直觉还是听从？
你的直觉在什么事上最准？

questions.title: 怎么学习，怎么放弃
questions.prompt: 你如何学习新东西？什么时候会放弃？举一个你学会的和一个放弃的。
questions.hint: 写你的学习路径：看教程、找人、直接做、拖很久。
probes: 你放弃时通常怎么解释？
你学得最快的一次是什么？

questions.title: 意见不合
questions.prompt: 你和别人意见不合时怎么处理？你会被说服吗？举一次你改变立场的经历。
questions.hint: 写你争论时的语气和身体反应。
probes: 你争的是道理还是输赢？
你有没有表面同意、心里不服？

questions.title: 你知道自己有什么偏见
questions.prompt: 你自知有哪些认知偏差？（确认偏误、沉没成本、讨好、灾难化、非黑即白……）
questions.hint: 写你被抓包过的那个。
probes: 谁提醒过你？
你为此损失过什么？

questions.title: 计划与执行
questions.prompt: 你怎么做计划？年计划、月计划、待办清单，完成率大概多少？
questions.hint: 写你实际用的工具和方法。
probes: 计划完不成时你怎么对自己？
你是计划型还是临场型？

questions.title: 沉没成本
questions.prompt: 你有没有该放手却没放手的事？（工作、关系、项目、一件东西）为什么放不下？
questions.hint: 写你继续投入的理由，和真实理由。
probes: 你最后怎么处理的？
你现在还在其中吗？

questions.title: 你的人生算法
questions.prompt: 如果你的人生是一条算法，它的目标函数是什么？约束条件是什么？
questions.hint: 目标函数：你实际在最大化的东西（不是嘴上说的）。约束：你不能牺牲的、不能突破的。
probes: 这个算法是谁给你写的？
你想改写哪一行？

zh.title: 关系网络与他者视角
zh.subtitle: 你是由谁组成的
zh.why: 一个人不是孤岛，是几张关系网的交叉点。这一章画出你的人物地图，也收集「别人眼里的你」——它能校正你的自我叙述。

questions.title: 生命里最重要的七个人
questions.prompt: 列出你生命中最重要的七个人（可以用代号）。每个人一句话：他是谁、你们什么关系、你欠他什么/他欠你什么。
questions.hint: 包括活着和离开的人。写你想到名字时的第一感觉。
probes: 谁是你不用解释就能懂的人？
谁是你最想让他骄傲的人？

questions.title: 现在最亲近的人
questions.prompt: 你现在最亲近的人是谁？多久见一次？聊什么？不聊什么？
questions.hint: 写最近一次见面的细节。
probes: 你们怎么表达关心？
你有什么事不会告诉他/她？

questions.title: 断交与失联
questions.prompt: 有没有断交或失联的重要的人？为什么？你现在还会想起吗？
questions.hint: 写最后一次对话。
probes: 如果对方联系你，你会回吗？
你后悔吗？

questions.title: 谁懂你，谁不懂
questions.prompt: 谁最懂你？谁最不懂你？谁最怕你？谁最爱你？
questions.hint: 可以重复，也可以写「没有人」。
probes: 被懂的感觉是什么样的？
你希望谁更懂你？

questions.title: 你在朋友中的角色
questions.prompt: 你在朋友中通常扮演什么角色？（组织者、倾听者、开心果、军师、消失的人、救火队……）
questions.hint: 写一个具体场景：朋友出事时你做什么。
probes: 你喜欢这个角色吗？
你有没有当过被照顾的那个？

questions.title: 感谢、道歉与拒绝
questions.prompt: 你如何表达感谢、道歉、拒绝？各举一个真实例子，写出你的原话。
questions.hint: 原话很重要，数字人的语气就藏在这里。
probes: 你说「不」难吗？
你道歉时会解释吗？

questions.title: 人情债与未说出口的话
questions.prompt: 你有没有人情债，或未说出口的话？对谁？
questions.hint: 写那个你想起会沉默的人。
probes: 你打算说吗？
如果不说，会怎样？

questions.title: 三封不必寄出的信
questions.prompt: 如果给三个人各写一句话（不必寄出），你会写给谁、说什么？
questions.hint: 一句话就够。
probes: 为什么是这三个人？
写完后你什么感觉？

questions.title: 你希望被怎么记住
questions.prompt: 你希望别人怎么记住你？你觉得别人实际会怎么记住你？
questions.hint: 写两句：理想版和现实版。
probes: 这两句差在哪里？
你能接受现实版吗？

questions.title: 最近一次感到被爱
questions.prompt: 你最近一次真切地感到被爱是什么时候？对方做了什么？
questions.hint: 写那个具体的动作或话。
probes: 你当时怎么回应？
你相信自己值得被爱吗？

zh.title: 意义、死亡与未完成
zh.subtitle: 如果时间不多了，你留下什么
zh.why: 最后一章把镜头拉远。一个人如何面对死亡、遗憾和未完成的事，决定了他/她真正看重什么——这也是数字人最该继承的部分。

questions.title: 人生的意义
questions.prompt: 你觉得人生的意义是什么？你的答案变过吗？
questions.hint: 可以写「没有意义」，也可以写一个具体的画面。
probes: 你什么时候最强烈地感到「活着真好」？
你什么时候觉得一切都没意义？

questions.title: 死亡
questions.prompt: 你怕死吗？你参加过葬礼、见过死亡吗？那之后你怎么看？
questions.hint: 写你离死亡最近的一次。
probes: 你相信死后还有吗？
你希望怎么离开？

questions.title: 只剩一年
questions.prompt: 如果你只剩一年，你会怎么过？会告诉谁、不告诉谁？
questions.hint: 写第一周、第一个月、最后一周。
probes: 你会辞职吗？
你最舍不得的是什么？

questions.title: 未完成的事
questions.prompt: 你最想完成、但还没开始的一件事是什么？为什么没开始？
questions.hint: 写那个你每年都想起一次的事。
probes: 最小的第一步是什么？
如果你永远不做，会后悔吗？

questions.title: 墓志铭
questions.prompt: 你希望墓志铭上写什么？你希望留下什么作品或影响？
questions.hint: 一句话就够。
probes: 你希望谁来看你？
你希望被记住多久？

questions.title: 未完成的对话
questions.prompt: 有没有一段「未完成的对话」——你想对某个人说、但一直没说的话？
questions.hint: 写一句开头就好。
probes: 为什么没说？
如果现在说，会怎样？

questions.title: 原谅
questions.prompt: 你原谅了谁？还没原谅谁？包括你自己吗？
questions.hint: 写那个你嘴上说算了、心里没过去的人。
probes: 原谅对你来说是什么？
你需要谁的原谅？

questions.title: 十年后的一天
questions.prompt: 十年后的你，理想状态是什么样？请具体到一天：住哪、和谁、做什么、几点起床。
questions.hint: 不要写「财务自由、环游世界」，写一个普通的周二。
probes: 那一天里，有什么是现在的你已经拥有的？
你愿意为那一天放弃什么？

questions.title: 被记住多久
questions.prompt: 你希望被谁记住、被记住多久？如果最终没有人记得你，你还觉得活过有意义吗？
questions.hint: 写你的真实感受。
probes: 你害怕被遗忘吗？
什么能证明你活过？

questions.title: 给 20 岁的自己
questions.prompt: 如果现在要给 20 岁的自己写三句话，你会写什么？
questions.hint: 写你真正想说的，不写正确的。
probes: 20 岁的你会听吗？
你现在最需要听到哪一句？

zh.title: 语言样本
zh.subtitle: 决定「像不像」的一章
zh.why: 很多数字人说得对，但不像。差别在语言：句子的长短、标点、口头禅、什么时候用表情、怎么骂人、怎么安慰。这一章请尽量贴原文，不要润色。

questions.title: 三段真实消息
questions.prompt: 贴三段你真实发过的消息：给朋友、给工作对象、给家人各一段（可脱敏，但保留语气和标点）。
questions.hint: 从聊天记录里复制，不要重写。长短、错别字、表情都保留。
probes: 你对三种人说话最大的差别是什么？
你会用语音吗？

questions.title: 一段你写过的文字
questions.prompt: 贴一段你写过的文字：日记、朋友圈、邮件、文章、备忘录都行。
questions.hint: 选你自己满意的，或最能代表你的。
probes: 你写东西时会改几遍？
你写作时和说话时像吗？

questions.title: 你的声音
questions.prompt: 你的说话特征：语速、音量、口音、停顿、爱说的词、笑的声音。如果方便，录一段 60 秒的自我介绍放在项目里，并写下文件名。
questions.hint: 不录也可以。写「我说话像……」的比喻。
probes: 你紧张时声音会变吗？
别人能听出你的情绪吗？

questions.title: 四种情境的原话
questions.prompt: 你生气时、安慰人时、撒娇/示弱时、拒绝人时，各会怎么说？请写原话。
questions.hint: 四种各一到两句。想象你正对着那个人说。
probes: 哪一句最不像你？
你有没有一句「万能回复」？

questions.title: 表情与标点
questions.prompt: 你常用哪些 emoji/表情包？你最常用的三个表情是什么？你打字爱用什么标点？
questions.hint: 截图或描述都可以。
probes: 你会用句号吗？
你发表情是礼貌还是真情绪？

questions.title: 你讨厌别人怎么说话
questions.prompt: 你讨厌别人怎么说话？（语气、词、腔调、句式）请举例子。
questions.hint: 写那种一听到就烦的说法。
probes: 你自己会这样说话吗？
你最讨厌被怎么称呼？

zh.title: 终局校验
zh.subtitle: 写下你的使用说明书
zh.why: 最后几题不是回忆，是校准。你亲手写下「怎样才算像我」「什么绝对不能说」，数字人就有了边界。这一章也会成为校验考试的评分标准。

questions.title: 你的使用说明书
questions.prompt: 别人要怎么和你相处？怎么道歉你会接受？怎么拒绝你，你不会受伤？你需要空间时，别人该怎么做？
questions.hint: 像给新同事或伴侣写一份说明书。
probes: 你最讨厌的关心方式是什么？
你难受时希望别人做点什么，还是什么都别做？

questions.title: 最容易被误解的地方
questions.prompt: 你最容易被人误解的地方是什么？为什么？
questions.hint: 写那个你解释了无数次、还是没人懂的点。
probes: 你希望别人怎么理解你？
你会为了不被误解而改变吗？

questions.title: 关闭、炸毛、逃离
questions.prompt: 什么会让你瞬间关闭、炸毛或想逃离？请各举一个具体触发点。
questions.hint: 写身体信号和你的第一反应。
probes: 触发之后你通常多久恢复？
有人知道怎么把你拉回来吗？

questions.title: 最近改变的主意
questions.prompt: 你最近一次改变主意是什么事？是什么让你改变的？
questions.hint: 大小都行。
probes: 你容易改变主意吗？
什么事你绝不会改？

questions.title: 只保留三句话
questions.prompt: 如果数字人只能保留你的三句话，你选哪三句？
questions.hint: 可以是口头禅、人生信条、或你常对别人说的话。
probes: 为什么是这三句？
这三句能代表你吗？

questions.title: 数字人绝对不要做
questions.prompt: 你希望数字人绝对不要说什么、做什么？（语气、内容、承诺、称呼、建议方式）
questions.hint: 写红线。比如「不要叫我亲爱的」「不要替我答应任何事」「不要给鸡汤」。
probes: 如果它越界了，你希望它怎么补救？
有哪些话题它应该直接回避？

questions.title: 怎么判断「像我」
questions.prompt: 你怎么判断一个回答「像我」？给出三个标准，按重要性排序。
questions.hint: 比如：会用我的词、不会过度解释、先说结论、承认不知道。
probes: 哪个标准最重要？
哪种「像」其实是刻板印象？

questions.title: 如果它比你更懂你
questions.prompt: 如果有一天，数字人比你更懂你，你会害怕还是高兴？为什么？
questions.hint: 写你的真实感受。
probes: 你希望它替你做什么决定？
你绝对不让它替你做什么决定？

en.title: Where You Are Now
en.subtitle: Put yourself back in this moment
en.why: The easiest mistake for a digital twin is to have opinions but no life. This chapter puts your body, your time, your money and your days in first. They set the ground you speak from and where the tiredness comes from.

questions.title: Three sentences
questions.prompt: Introduce who you are now in three sentences. First: who you are (identity, roles). Second: what you are doing (work, what your life centres on). Third: what you care about most right now, what you cannot put down.
questions.hint: Don't write a CV. Write what you tell yourself at 2 a.m. Three sentences is enough, no need to expand.
probes: If you could keep only one, which one?
Which of the three sounds least like you?

questions.title: Basic coordinates
questions.prompt: Year and place of birth, where you live now, who you live with, what work you do, native language, dialect, other languages, family structure (parents, siblings, marriage, children).
questions.hint: Like filling in a file only you will read. A list of facts is enough.
probes: How many times have you moved in the past ten years? Which move hurt most?
Where you live now: which corner of it is most like you?

questions.title: An ordinary workday
questions.prompt: From opening your eyes to closing them, how does an ordinary workday go? Write it in time order: waking up, phone, food, commute, work, time alone, bed.
questions.hint: The more trivial the better. Write what you actually do, not what you should do.
probes: Which moment is most like you?
Which moment do you most want to escape?

questions.title: An ordinary weekend
questions.prompt: An unscheduled weekend: how do you spend it? With whom, where, doing what? If the weekend is arranged for you, how does that feel?
questions.hint: Write the most recent real weekend, not the ideal one.
probes: Roughly what is your ratio of alone time to social time?
How do you usually feel when the weekend ends?

questions.title: The body, this machine
questions.prompt: Your body right now: sleep, energy, exercise, pain or chronic problems, food, anything off in a check-up. What is your relationship with your body like?
questions.hint: The body is the most honest biography. Write concrete numbers: what time you sleep, how many hours, how often you exercise.
probes: Is there a part of your body that makes you sigh just thinking about it?
When did you last feel your body was doing well?

questions.title: Where money sits
questions.prompt: Your money now: where income comes from and roughly how it breaks down, debt, how safe your savings make you feel, your last big expense, the purchase you most regret.
questions.hint: Exact numbers are not needed; ranges and proportions are fine. What matters is how you feel about money, not the ledger.
probes: When did you last lose sleep over money?
If your income stopped tomorrow, how long could you last?

questions.title: A pie chart of time
questions.prompt: Over the past year, what have you spent your time on? Give a rough pie chart in percentages, and mark which slice you actually want to be spending it on.
questions.hint: For example: work 50%, commute 8%, scrolling 12%, family 10%, yourself 5%.
probes: Which slice surprises you most?
If you had to cut one slice, which one?

questions.title: The last real laugh, the last time you cried
questions.prompt: When did you last laugh for real, and at what? When did you last cry, or almost cry, and why?
questions.hint: Give the specific scene and the line that made you laugh or cry.
probes: Are you quicker to laugh or quicker to cry?
Do you cry in front of other people?

questions.title: If your life right now were a film
questions.prompt: What is the title? What is the image in the first scene? If you had to write one tagline for it, what would it be?
questions.hint: Your first reaction is the most accurate. Don't think too long.
probes: What genre is this film?
How do you want it to end?

questions.title: What the person who knows you best would say
questions.prompt: The person closest to you, the one who knows you best: how would they describe your state right now? Write in their voice, not yours.
questions.hint: Picture them sitting across from you, describing you to a stranger.
probes: What are they most worried about for you?
Which part of what they say would you deny?

en.title: Life timeline
en.subtitle: Ten anchor points, walking you through it again
en.why: Character doesn't grow out of nowhere. It is the posture left by a series of concrete events. This chapter rebuilds your timeline out of scenes, not conclusions. A digital twin's memory can only come from here.

questions.title: Earliest memory
questions.prompt: What is your earliest memory? Roughly how old were you? The image, the smell, the sound, the light, who was there, how you felt.
questions.hint: You don't need to be sure of the age. Even if it is just one image or one smell, write it down.
probes: In that scene, what would you most want to change?
Who did you later tell this memory to?

questions.title: Childhood (roughly 7 to 12)
questions.prompt: What was home like then? What was school like? Who was your best friend? What were you most afraid of? What were you proudest of?
questions.hint: One specific afternoon or one incident is far more useful than 'my childhood was happy'.
probes: What kind of kid did you think you were then?
Was there an adult who really saw you?

questions.title: One thing that changed how you saw yourself
questions.prompt: In childhood or your teens, was there something that changed how you saw yourself? It can be for the better or the worse.
questions.hint: For example a competition, being wrongly blamed, changing schools, being praised.
probes: If that hadn't happened, who would you have become?
Do you still believe the conclusion you drew then?

questions.title: Adolescence (roughly 13 to 18)
questions.prompt: Changes in your body, rebellion, secrets, the first time you liked someone, the first time you were turned down, your relationship with your parents. Pick what you remember most clearly.
questions.hint: You don't need to cover everything. Write the scene that still makes you blush or tightens your chest.
probes: What was your biggest secret then?
What did you rebel against? What happened?

questions.title: The first big choice
questions.prompt: The college entrance exam, choosing a major, which city to go to, your first job. What was your first real, significant choice? What did you choose, who made the decision, and what did it cost?
questions.hint: What matters is not whether the outcome was good, but how you thought at the time and who influenced you.
probes: If you could do it again, would you choose the other one?
What does that choice still affect now?

questions.title: First time leaving home (roughly 18 to 22)
questions.prompt: When did you first leave home for a long stretch? Where did you go? Who did you meet? What did you learn? What did you lose?
questions.hint: Write something that could only have happened because you left home.
probes: When did you start missing home?
When did you first feel you had grown up?

questions.title: First real independence, first big failure (roughly 22 to 28)
questions.prompt: What was living on your own for the first time like? What did your first job teach you? What was your first big failure, and how did you get through it?
questions.hint: You can write about two jobs, a break-up, an exam, a start-up. Be specific.
probes: What did that failure change in you?
Who caught you during that stretch?

questions.title: 28 to now: three turning points
questions.prompt: From 28 to now, what have been the three most important turning points in your life? Changing cities, changing jobs, marriage, divorce, illness, a death in the family, starting something. How did you decide each time?
questions.hint: Write them in order. If you can't go on, write the headlines and add detail later.
probes: Which one did you choose, and which one was you being pushed?
Do the three have anything in common?

questions.title: The lowest point
questions.prompt: When was the lowest point of your life so far? What happened? How did you get through each day? Who was there? How did you come out of it?
questions.hint: You can blur the details. If writing it now hurts, one line is enough: 'there was a stretch when...'
probes: What did you most need to hear then?
Did you think about giving up? What kept you?

questions.title: The highest point
questions.prompt: What was the high point of your life? What happened? How did you feel at the time? Why didn't it continue?
questions.hint: A high point doesn't have to be worldly success. It could be an afternoon when you felt whole.
probes: Who did you most want to tell at that moment?
Do you still think about it?

questions.title: Life curve: five points
questions.prompt: If you drew your life as a curve, age on the horizontal axis and state on the vertical, write five key points: age, state, and one word to name it.
questions.hint: For example: age 6, high, my grandmother's house; 16, low, turned down; 24, high, first job.
probes: Which way is the curve trending now?
Where do you want the next point to be?

questions.title: The parallel life
questions.prompt: Is there a 'you that almost was'? Which step did it come down to? Do you still think about that person?
questions.hint: It could be another major, another city, another relationship, another profession.
probes: Do you regret it?
What does that version of you have that you lack now?

en.title: Family and attachment
en.subtitle: The first way you learned to love
en.why: How a person handles conflict, how they ask for what they need, how they face being left: most of the first draft was written at the childhood dinner table. This chapter is not putting your parents on trial. It is seeing what you inherited and what you refused.

questions.title: Father
questions.prompt: What kind of person is your father? Describe him in three words. What is the one thing he did that affected you most? Are you like him?
questions.hint: Write concrete images: his catchphrase, his hands, what he looks like when he is angry.
probes: What do you most want from him?
Which part of him do you least want to become?

questions.title: Mother
questions.prompt: What kind of person is your mother? Describe her in three words. What is the one thing she did that affected you most? Are you like her?
questions.hint: Again, concrete images rather than summaries like 'she had a hard life'.
probes: What do you most want from her?
Which part of her do you least want to become?

questions.title: House rules, taboos, and things you don't say
questions.prompt: What were the stated and unstated rules in your home? Which topics could not be raised? Which feelings were not allowed? What mistakes got you punished?
questions.hint: For example: no crying, no talking back, silent treatment when your grades were bad, kids don't ask about money.
probes: Which rule did you break? What happened?
Are those rules still in you now?

questions.title: You cried, you failed an exam, you broke something
questions.prompt: When you were a kid and you cried, failed an exam, or got into trouble, how did your family usually handle it? Give one real example of each.
questions.hint: Focus on the adults' first reaction, and yours.
probes: What did you want them to do then?
How do you treat yourself now when you are sad?

questions.title: What you inherited and what you refused
questions.prompt: What did you inherit from your family? Habits, beliefs, fears, your body, the way you talk. What did you explicitly refuse to inherit?
questions.hint: Write three of each. The part you refused: have you managed it?
probes: Was there a moment you noticed you were becoming more and more like my mother, my father?
What has refusing to inherit cost you?

questions.title: Your relationship with your parents now
questions.prompt: How often do you talk now? What do you talk about, what don't you? What have you done for them? What have they done for you?
questions.hint: Write about your last phone call: what was said and what the mood was.
probes: Is there something you want to say to them but haven't?
What are they most worried about for you now?

questions.title: The secret the family doesn't mention
questions.prompt: Is there something in your family that everyone knows and no one mentions? Or a secret?
questions.hint: You can skip this. You can write it vaguely, e.g. 'a stretch of time about my uncle'.
probes: How did it affect you?
Will you carry it into your own family?

questions.title: The way of raising kids you don't want to repeat
questions.prompt: If you have children, or will, what is the parenting you absolutely don't want to repeat? What do you want to manage to do?
questions.hint: Write concrete behaviour, not slogans.
probes: Do you think you can do it?
What is the line you are most afraid will come out of your mouth?

questions.title: The moment your parents became ordinary people
questions.prompt: When did you first realise your parents were just ordinary people, that they make mistakes and that they will die? What happened?
questions.hint: It might have been an illness, an argument, or a time you found out they didn't know either.
probes: Did your attitude toward them change after that?
How do you understand them now?

questions.title: What home is
questions.prompt: 'Home': what is it to you? If home were a person, who would it be, what would they be like, what would they say to you?
questions.hint: Use a metaphor, not a definition.
probes: Do you have the feeling of home now? Where?
What does your ideal home look like?

en.title: Behavioural evidence
en.subtitle: Don't describe yourself. Say what happened.
en.why: 'I'm fairly introverted' is almost useless for modelling. 'Ninety minutes into a party I go stand on the balcony for ten' is not. This chapter locates your character through scenes and counter-examples, not labels.

questions.title: Social battery
questions.prompt: When you are with a group of people, how does your battery usually change?
questions.hint: Think of a specific group: colleagues, friends, family. It can differ by group; write the average first.
probes: Which kind of person drains you most?
Which kind of person lets you stop performing?
questions.left: Three hours alone to recharge
questions.right: The more people, the more energy

questions.title: Need for order
questions.prompt: How much does your life need plans and order?
questions.hint: Look at your desk, your luggage, your to-do list, how you travel. Not at your ideals.
probes: Where must things be tidy? Where can they be a mess?
When a plan gets disrupted, what is your first reaction?
questions.left: Casual; plans are made to be broken
questions.right: Everything must be scheduled in advance

questions.title: Emotional range
questions.prompt: How far does your mood swing?
questions.hint: Think back over the last month: how many days were clearly off your normal?
probes: What most easily lifts you? What most easily pulls you down?
Can other people tell?
questions.left: Like a lake, rarely a wave
questions.right: Like the sea, obvious highs and lows

questions.title: Openness
questions.prompt: Faced with something new, a new restaurant, a new idea, a new place, a new tool, what is your usual attitude?
questions.hint: Think separately about food, play, methods at work, values. You may be open in only some of them.
probes: What is one new thing you tried on your own recently?
What new thing will you absolutely not touch?
questions.left: Familiar is fine; don't fuss
questions.right: Novelty first; try it and see

questions.title: Sharpness
questions.prompt: When you have to say something true that might make someone uncomfortable, how do you usually handle it?
questions.hint: Think of the last time you pointed out someone's problem, or held it in.
probes: Have you hurt someone? How did you deal with it afterwards?
Do you want people to tell you the truth?
questions.left: Keep the peace; say it only if you must
questions.right: Say it straight first, then deal with feelings

questions.title: Ninety minutes into a party
questions.prompt: A party is ninety minutes in. Where are you? What are you doing? What is going on in your head?
questions.hint: Write your body: checking your phone, on the balcony, doing the dishes, finding someone for a one-on-one.
probes: When do you leave early? How do you say it?
Who do you usually end up with the longest at a party?

questions.title: What you promise others, what you promise yourself
questions.prompt: What you promise other people and what you promise yourself: which is easier to keep? Give one recent example of each.
questions.hint: For example 'rewriting a colleague's proposal' versus 'writing something for myself'.
probes: When you break a promise to yourself, how do you explain it?
When someone breaks a promise to you, what do you think?

questions.title: Desk, room, phone home screen
questions.prompt: What do your desk, your room, and your phone's home screen look like right now? Where is the order, where is the chaos?
questions.hint: You can take a photo and then describe it in words. Don't tidy up first.
probes: Does your mess follow a pattern?
What happens if someone moves your things?

questions.title: The last time you were really angry
questions.prompt: When were you last really angry, or badly irritated? What set it off? What did you do? How did it end?
questions.hint: Write your body's first reaction: face hot, hands shaking, wanting to throw something, wanting to disappear.
probes: What is your pattern when angry: explode, go cold, argue it out, or keep score?
What did you want the other person to do then?

questions.title: The last time you were really sad
questions.prompt: When were you last really sad? How did you handle it? Did you find someone, or carry it yourself?
questions.hint: If you can't cry, write the blocked-up feeling instead.
probes: Who do you most not want to see you sad?
What actually comforts you?

questions.title: Being alone
questions.prompt: Do you need time alone? How much? What do you turn into without it? What do you usually do alone?
questions.hint: Distinguish being by yourself from time that is really yours.
probes: What do you think about most when you are alone?
Are you afraid of being alone?

questions.title: Praise and criticism
questions.prompt: How do you react when someone praises you? And when someone criticises you? Give one real recent example of each.
questions.hint: Write what you say out loud and what you think. They may differ.
probes: Which compliment have you kept for a long time?
Which criticism still stings?

questions.title: What you can't stand
questions.prompt: What can't you stand in other people? Do you have that problem yourself?
questions.hint: Write three. The third is usually the hardest to admit.
probes: What do you do when you meet this kind of person?
Has anyone ever told you that you are exactly that kind of person?

questions.title: You in three circles
questions.prompt: If three people from different circles, say family, colleagues, old friends, each summed you up in one sentence, what would they say? Which sentence is most accurate?
questions.hint: Write their actual words. Don't polish them on their behalf.
probes: In which circle are you most relaxed?
Put together, do they sound like you?

en.title: Values and beliefs
en.subtitle: What you are paying for
en.why: Values aren't the words you pick on a questionnaire. They are what you actually protect in a conflict, at a cost, when something has to give. This chapter is after your bottom lines, your ranking, and what you will pay for them.

questions.title: Three bottom lines
questions.prompt: What are things you absolutely will not do? List three, and say why.
questions.hint: Don't write murder, things nobody should do. Write the ones that are yours, e.g. 'I don't badmouth a friend behind their back', 'I don't write things I don't believe for money'.
probes: Has anyone crossed your bottom line? How did you handle it?
Have you paid a price for holding a bottom line?

questions.title: A successful life
questions.prompt: What does a successful life look like to you? How far from it are you now?
questions.hint: Write the standard social answer first, then your own. They may not match.
probes: What do your parents think success is? Do you agree?
Are you afraid you will die without having succeeded?

questions.title: What money means to you
questions.prompt: What does money mean to you? How much counts as enough? What would you do for money, and what wouldn't you?
questions.hint: Write a concrete number, and the picture of a life behind that number.
probes: When you had no money, what were you most afraid of?
Have you seen money change someone?

questions.title: Ranking and sacrifice
questions.prompt: Freedom, security, achievement, relationships, meaning: put them in order. Then say when you last sacrificed one for another.
questions.hint: Rank by instinct first, then check whether your recent actual choices match.
probes: Does your ranking conflict with your parents' or your partner's?
If you could keep only one, which?

questions.title: What you believe
questions.prompt: What do you believe in? Religion, philosophy, science, fate, karma, luck, effort. How do you explain bad things happening to good people?
questions.hint: If you have no faith, you can write what you don't believe in.
probes: Have you ever prayed? When?
Have you had a moment of 'this was meant to happen'?

questions.title: Your strongest position
questions.prompt: On a political or social issue, what is your strongest position? What would you pay for it?
questions.hint: You can skip this. Write what you actually think; no need to be politically correct.
probes: Does anyone around you hold the opposite view? How do you get along?
Have you lost anything because of a position you held?

questions.title: Respect and contempt
questions.prompt: What kind of people do you respect? What kind do you look down on? Which side are you closer to?
questions.hint: Write three kinds of people each, then one specific name or figure.
probes: What do the people you respect have in common?
Have you ever done something you look down on in others?

questions.title: A belief that changed recently
questions.prompt: Is there a view you once held firmly that changed recently? What changed it?
questions.hint: Work, love, money, human nature, yourself. Any of them.
probes: Was the change painful?
What are you still sure of now?

questions.title: The thing you most regret
questions.prompt: What is the most immoral or the most regretted thing you have done? You can blur the details. How did you face it afterwards?
questions.hint: You can skip this. Write the part you are willing to write.
probes: Did you apologise?
Have you forgiven yourself?

questions.title: Three rules for living
questions.prompt: If you could teach only three rules of life to someone younger, what would they be? One sentence each.
questions.hint: Write the three you actually live by, not the three you wish you lived by.
probes: Which one took you the longest to learn?
Which one can't you manage even now?

en.title: Love and intimacy
en.subtitle: How you come close, and how you back away
en.why: Intimate relationships are where character hides least: how you ask for what you need, how you handle conflict, when you run. This chapter decides whether the digital twin feels like you in emotional scenes.

questions.title: Relationship history
questions.prompt: Your romantic history: how many important relationships? How did each start, how did each end, what did you learn?
questions.hint: No need for gossipy detail. Write the pattern: who you are always drawn to, and where you always get stuck.
probes: Is there one you still haven't got over?
What is the mistake you most easily make in a relationship?

questions.title: How you know you've fallen
questions.prompt: How do you know that you have fallen for someone? What signals does your body give, and what does your head?
questions.hint: Write concrete signals: wanting to share something, checking your phone over and over, your body relaxing, starting to be afraid.
probes: Do you say it first?
What do you turn into when you love someone?

questions.title: What kind of love you need
questions.prompt: What do you most need in a relationship? What are you most afraid will happen?
questions.hint: Need: company, space, being affirmed, stability, passion, being understood. Most afraid of: being abandoned, being controlled, being seen through, losing yourself.
probes: Have you ever been ashamed of needing too much?
Have you ever got the love you wanted?

questions.title: You in a conflict
questions.prompt: When you clash with a partner or a close friend, what are you like? Pressing for an answer, running, going cold, erupting, reasoning, giving in. Take the most recent time.
questions.hint: Write what happened in the first minute, and what happened on day three.
probes: How do you make up? Who gives in first?
What can't you stand the other person doing in a conflict?

questions.title: How you show love, how you show displeasure
questions.prompt: How do you show love? Does the other person receive it? How do you show displeasure?
questions.hint: Write your love language: doing things, giving things, physical touch, spending time, words.
probes: What expression of yours gets misread most?
How do you want the other person to show it to you?

questions.title: Jealousy
questions.prompt: Do you get jealous? What triggers it? How do you handle it?
questions.hint: Write the most recent time, including what you said and what you didn't.
probes: Do you go through their phone?
When jealous, do you want to control or to run?

questions.title: What you hide in a relationship
questions.prompt: In an intimate relationship, what is the biggest thing you have hidden, or the biggest lie? You can name the type without the detail.
questions.hint: You can skip this. Feelings you never said out loud count too.
probes: Why don't you say it?
What would happen if they knew?

questions.title: Loyalty, boundaries, and the rest
questions.prompt: What do you think about loyalty, boundaries, open relationships, long distance, age gaps?
questions.hint: Write what you actually think. No need to be correct.
probes: Where are your boundaries?
Have you crossed someone else's?

questions.title: Your relationship status now
questions.prompt: Your relationship now: what satisfies you, what you want to change, what you don't dare say.
questions.hint: If you are single, you can write about your relationship with yourself, your family, your friends.
probes: When did you last feel close to someone?
What are you waiting for?

questions.title: If you end up alone
questions.prompt: If you ended up living alone, how would you do it? What are you most afraid of?
questions.hint: Write the picture: where you would live, what you would do each day, who you would see.
probes: Could you live well on your own?
Are you more afraid of loneliness, or of how others see you?

en.title: Work and ambition
en.subtitle: The shape you want to leave in the world
en.why: Work is not just income. It is how you wrestle with reality. This chapter records your abilities, your ambition, your failure patterns, and the tone you actually use when you talk about work.

questions.title: Career path
questions.prompt: Your career path: for each job or project, why you went, why you left, what you took with you.
questions.hint: List them in order. Write the real reason you quit.
probes: Which stretch was most like you?
Which career choice do you most regret?

questions.title: What you're best at and what you hate
questions.prompt: What are you best at, the thing people come to you for help with? What are you worst at, and what do you hate most?
questions.hint: Write specific abilities, not job titles. For example 'turning a mess of requirements into a process' rather than 'product manager'.
probes: How did you get good at it?
Has anyone praised you for something you don't actually rate in yourself?

questions.title: Ambition
questions.prompt: How big is your ambition? What would you sacrifice for it? Who do you secretly want to become?
questions.hint: Write the version you don't quite dare say out loud.
probes: Are you afraid of succeeding?
If you stayed ordinary your whole life, could you accept that?

questions.title: Facing authority
questions.prompt: How do you handle bosses, clients, authority? Give one time you pushed back, or one time you gave in.
questions.hint: Write what you said out loud and what you thought.
probes: Are you afraid of authority?
What would you be like once you are the authority?

questions.title: Facing failure
questions.prompt: What is the biggest professional failure you have been through? Your first reaction, how you recovered, how you see it now.
questions.hint: Write how you explained it to other people at the time.
probes: Did you actually use what you learned from it?
Would you try again?

questions.title: Grinding, lying flat, and boundaries
questions.prompt: Do you grind? Do you fake it? What do you make of lying flat? Where is the line between work and life?
questions.hint: Write your actual hours, not your attitude.
probes: Do you still think about work after you leave?
Do you feel guilty taking leave?

questions.title: The work you're proudest of
questions.prompt: What is the work or project you are proudest of? Why that one?
questions.hint: It can be a job, or a private project, an article, a meal.
probes: Does it still exist?
What do others say about it?

questions.title: If you were financially free tomorrow
questions.prompt: If you were financially free tomorrow, what would you do? Would you still work? How would you spend a day?
questions.hint: Write the first week, then the first year.
probes: Which part of your current work could money not buy?
Who would you leave?

questions.title: Money habits
questions.prompt: Your money habits: tracking spending, investing, borrowing, splitting bills, treating people, how you and your partner manage money.
questions.hint: Write what you actually do, including the part you are ashamed of.
probes: How did your parents spend? Who do you take after?
What is the best-value thing you have bought?

questions.title: Your biggest fear about work
questions.prompt: What is your biggest fear about work? Being made redundant, being seen through, meaninglessness, falling behind your peers, having no body of work.
questions.hint: Write the thought that wakes you at night.
probes: When did this fear start?
What has it protected you from?

en.title: Desire and shadow
en.subtitle: The things you don't say at the dinner table
en.why: A digital twin built only from your bright side would read like a promo video. What actually makes it like you is the desire you're not proud of, the shame, the self-sabotage. Every question in this chapter can be skipped, and you can write only the part you're willing to write.

questions.title: What you want most and won't admit
questions.prompt: What do you want most that you can hardly admit to? (Being seen, being loved, beating someone, not having to try, being taken care of, revenge…)
questions.hint: Write the first reaction. There is no moral score here.
probes: If you got it, what then?
What have you done for it?

questions.title: What you most fear people finding out
questions.prompt: What do you most fear people discovering about you?
questions.hint: Write the point where, if someone saw through you, it would be over.
probes: Has anyone ever found out?
What do you cover it with?

questions.title: Envy
questions.prompt: Who did you last envy, and what for? What did you do about it?
questions.hint: Envy usually points at what you actually want.
probes: Have you ever admitted you were envious?
After the envy, do you want to work harder or tear it down?

questions.title: Shame
questions.prompt: Where does your shame come from? What is your most shameful memory? (You can blur it.)
questions.hint: You can skip this. Write the moment your body remembers.
probes: Who made you feel shame?
What still makes you flush now?

questions.title: Addiction and losing control
questions.prompt: Is there anything you're addicted to or have lost control of? (Phone, games, alcohol, shopping, work, relationships, sex, food, mood)
questions.hint: You can skip this. Write how you've tried to control it.
probes: What does it help you avoid?
Have you ever quit?

questions.title: Self-sabotage
questions.prompt: Do you wreck things for yourself at the critical moment? Usually how?
questions.hint: For example: procrastinating until the last minute, disappearing, saying something cutting, deliberately not sleeping.
probes: In that moment, what are you protecting?
How do you explain it afterward?

questions.title: The darkest thought
questions.prompt: What is the darkest thought you've had? (Hurting yourself, disappearing, revenge, wishing someone would disappear…) What do you do with it?
questions.hint: You can skip this. If you are in danger right now, contact someone you trust or a local crisis line first; this question can wait.
probes: When is the thought strongest?
What makes it recede?

questions.title: The biggest lie
questions.prompt: What is the biggest lie you've told? To whom? Why?
questions.hint: You can skip this. You can also write the lie you told yourself.
probes: Is the lie still going?
Do you regret it?

questions.title: The other you
questions.prompt: Is there another you, one that only shows up late at night, online, in front of strangers, or when drunk? What is that one like?
questions.hint: Write the difference between that version and the everyday one.
probes: Do you like that version?
Which one is more real?

questions.title: If no one would ever know
questions.prompt: If nothing you did would ever be known and there were no consequences, what would you do differently?
questions.hint: You can skip this. Write the first reaction.
probes: What does that say about what you hold down?
Is there one small thing you could do now?

en.title: Daily life and taste
en.subtitle: Your small gestures and quirks
en.why: Whether it feels like you often comes down to details: which punctuation you use, what time you shower, whether you avoid stepping on the lines. This chapter collects the things that look useless and sound most like you.

questions.title: Your phone
questions.prompt: What does your home screen look like? What are the five apps you use most? How much screen time? What is the last thing you do before sleep?
questions.hint: Write it straight, including the app you're embarrassed about.
probes: What is the first thing you do after waking?
Have you tried quitting your phone?

questions.title: Body habits
questions.prompt: Sleep position, first thing after waking, coffee/tea/cigarettes/alcohol, exercise, when you shower, the fixed small motions of your day.
questions.hint: Write your body's fixed routine, like a manual.
probes: Which habit do you most want to change?
Which habit would you never change?

questions.title: Taste
questions.prompt: Your style of dress, the object at home that is most like you, your favorite color/material/smell.
questions.hint: Write what you actually own, not what you'd like to own.
probes: What is the most “that's exactly you” thing you have ever bought?
What kind of taste do you hate?

questions.title: Music
questions.prompt: Three songs on repeat lately, one song that makes you cry, one song that represents you.
questions.hint: Song titles and artists; a line on how it feels is better still.
probes: When do you need music most?
Do you sing?

questions.title: Work that shaped you
questions.prompt: Films, books, games, shows: pick three that have shaped you. Why those?
questions.hint: Don't pick the highbrow ones. Pick the ones you actually remember.
probes: When did a work last hit you?
Do you rewatch the same one?

questions.title: Your sense of humor
questions.prompt: What makes you laugh? Tell one thing or joke you found funny recently. How do you joke around?
questions.hint: Just write what you said. Don't explain the punchline.
probes: What is your kind of humor: deadpan, cutting, self-deprecating, absurd, puns?
Who do you joke about?

questions.title: Speech habits
questions.prompt: Your catchphrases, how you type, the emoji/punctuation you favor, voice or text, whether you mix in English. Give three things you say often.
questions.hint: Open your chat history and copy three real lines; that's more accurate than memory.
probes: Does your typing change when you're angry?
Do you type “ha” or “hahaha”?

questions.title: Relaxing, rewards and punishment
questions.prompt: How do you relax? How do you reward yourself? How do you punish yourself?
questions.hint: Punishment might be no rest allowed, bingeing, staying up all night.
probes: When did you last really relax?
Do you think you deserve to rest?

questions.title: Collections, fixations and small quirks
questions.prompt: Do you collect things, have odd fixations or small quirks? (Collecting cups, things having to be straight, not stepping on the lines, reorganizing folders at midnight…)
questions.hint: The less useful, the better.
probes: When did these quirks start?
Does anyone know?

questions.title: The 15 minutes that are most yours
questions.prompt: Which 15 minutes of the day are most your own? What are you doing?
questions.hint: Write the exact time and place.
probes: What happens if those 15 minutes get interrupted?
Do you need more time like that?

en.title: Decisions and thinking
en.subtitle: How you choose, how you regret
en.why: A digital twin that can't make a judgment for you is just a chat toy. This chapter pulls out your decision algorithm: how you take in information, trust your gut, take risk, put things off, and regret.

questions.title: How a big decision gets made
questions.prompt: When you make a big decision, how does it usually go? (Gathering information, asking people, going on instinct, putting it off, making a list.) Use a real recent decision.
questions.hint: Write the whole path from the first thought to the final call, including the night you couldn't sleep.
probes: Whose voice do you end up following?
Any decision you regretted the moment it was made?

questions.title: The decision you most regret
questions.prompt: What decision do you most regret? If you could do it again, what would you choose?
questions.hint: Write the one that still comes back to you in the shower.
probes: What did you learn from it?
Would you really take the other road?

questions.title: Appetite for risk
questions.prompt: Are you cautious or a risk-taker? With money, with work, with love? Give one example of a risk you took.
questions.hint: The three can be completely different. Write them separately.
probes: What is the biggest risk you've taken?
Can you afford to lose?

questions.title: Instinct
questions.prompt: Do you trust your instincts? Has instinct ever saved you, or ruined you?
questions.hint: Write the body feeling: a tight stomach, a cold back, an unexplained calm.
probes: Do you usually ignore instinct or follow it?
What is your instinct most accurate about?

questions.title: How you learn, how you quit
questions.prompt: How do you learn something new? When do you give up? Give one thing you learned and one you quit.
questions.hint: Write your learning path: tutorials, finding someone, doing it straight away, putting it off for months.
probes: How do you usually explain a quit?
What did you learn fastest?

questions.title: When you disagree
questions.prompt: How do you handle disagreement? Can you be persuaded? Describe a time you changed your position.
questions.hint: Write your tone and what your body does when you argue.
probes: Are you arguing for the point or for winning?
Have you ever agreed out loud while not agreeing at all?

questions.title: The biases you know you have
questions.prompt: Which cognitive biases do you know you have? (Confirmation bias, sunk cost, people-pleasing, catastrophizing, all or nothing…)
questions.hint: Write the one you've been caught on.
probes: Who pointed it out?
What has it cost you?

questions.title: Plans and follow-through
questions.prompt: How do you plan? Year plans, month plans, to-do lists: what share actually gets done?
questions.hint: Write the tools and methods you actually use.
probes: What do you do to yourself when the plan falls apart?
Are you a planner or do you improvise?

questions.title: Sunk cost
questions.prompt: Is there something you should have let go of and didn't? (A job, a relationship, a project, an object.) Why couldn't you?
questions.hint: Write the reason you gave for putting more in, and the real reason.
probes: How did it end?
Are you still in it?

questions.title: Your life algorithm
questions.prompt: If your life were an algorithm, what would its objective function be? What are its constraints?
questions.hint: Objective function: what you are actually maximizing, not what you say. Constraints: what you won't sacrifice, what you won't cross.
probes: Who wrote this algorithm for you?
Which line would you rewrite?

en.title: People and perception
en.subtitle: Who you are made of
en.why: A person isn't an island; a person is where a few webs of relationships cross. This chapter draws your map of people, and collects you as others see you, which can correct your own account of yourself.

questions.title: The seven most important people in your life
questions.prompt: List the seven most important people in your life (initials are fine). One line each: who they are, what you are to each other, what you owe them or they owe you.
questions.hint: Include the living and the gone. Write the first feeling that comes with the name.
probes: Who understands you without needing an explanation?
Who do you most want to make proud?

questions.title: The person closest to you now
questions.prompt: Who is closest to you now? How often do you see them? What do you talk about, and what don't you?
questions.hint: Write the details of the last time you met.
probes: How do you show each other you care?
What would you never tell them?

questions.title: Cut off, out of touch
questions.prompt: Is there someone important you cut off or lost touch with? Why? Do you still think about them?
questions.hint: Write the last conversation.
probes: If they reached out, would you answer?
Do you regret it?

questions.title: Who gets you, who doesn't
questions.prompt: Who understands you best? Who least? Who is most afraid of you? Who loves you most?
questions.hint: The answers can repeat. “No one” is allowed.
probes: What does being understood feel like?
Who do you wish understood you better?

questions.title: Your role among friends
questions.prompt: What role do you usually play among friends? (The organizer, the listener, the one who keeps it light, the strategist, the one who disappears, the one who puts out fires…)
questions.hint: Write one specific scene: what you do when a friend is in trouble.
probes: Do you like that role?
Have you ever been the one taken care of?

questions.title: Thanks, apology, refusal
questions.prompt: How do you say thank you, apologize, and turn someone down? Give a real example of each, in your exact words.
questions.hint: The exact words matter. That's where the twin's tone lives.
probes: Is saying “no” hard for you?
Do you explain when you apologize?

questions.title: Debts of kindness, words never said
questions.prompt: Do you owe someone a debt of kindness, or carry words you never said? To whom?
questions.hint: Write the person you go quiet thinking about.
probes: Do you plan to say it?
If you don't, what happens?

questions.title: Three letters you don't have to send
questions.prompt: If you wrote one line each to three people (they don't have to be sent), who would they be, and what would you say?
questions.hint: One line is enough.
probes: Why these three?
How do you feel after writing them?

questions.title: How you want to be remembered
questions.prompt: How do you want people to remember you? How do you think they actually will?
questions.hint: Two lines: the ideal version and the real one.
probes: Where do the two lines part ways?
Can you live with the real one?

questions.title: The last time you felt loved
questions.prompt: When did you last truly feel loved? What did the other person do?
questions.hint: Write the specific gesture or sentence.
probes: How did you respond?
Do you believe you deserve to be loved?

en.title: Meaning and mortality
en.subtitle: If time were short, what would you leave
en.why: The last chapter pulls the camera back. How a person faces death, regret and unfinished things shows what they actually value, and that is what the digital twin should inherit most.

questions.title: The meaning of life
questions.prompt: What do you think the meaning of life is? Has your answer changed?
questions.hint: “There's no meaning” is a fine answer. So is one concrete image.
probes: When have you felt most strongly that being alive is good?
When does everything feel meaningless?

questions.title: Death
questions.prompt: Are you afraid of dying? Have you been to a funeral, seen a death? How did you see things after?
questions.hint: Write the time you came closest to death.
probes: Do you believe anything comes after?
How do you want to go?

questions.title: One year left
questions.prompt: If you had one year left, how would you spend it? Who would you tell, and who wouldn't you?
questions.hint: Write the first week, the first month, the last week.
probes: Would you quit your job?
What would you least want to leave?

questions.title: Unfinished
questions.prompt: What is the one thing you most want to finish and haven't started? Why not?
questions.hint: Write the thing you remember once a year.
probes: What is the smallest first step?
If you never do it, will you regret it?

questions.title: Epitaph
questions.prompt: What do you want on your gravestone? What work or effect do you want to leave?
questions.hint: One line is enough.
probes: Who do you want to visit you?
How long do you want to be remembered?

questions.title: The unfinished conversation
questions.prompt: Is there an unfinished conversation, something you've wanted to say to someone and never have?
questions.hint: Just write the opening line.
probes: Why didn't you say it?
If you said it now, what would happen?

questions.title: Forgiveness
questions.prompt: Who have you forgiven? Who haven't you? Does that include yourself?
questions.hint: Write the person you say you're over and aren't.
probes: What is forgiveness to you?
Whose forgiveness do you need?

questions.title: A day ten years from now
questions.prompt: Ten years from now, what does your ideal look like? Get down to one day: where you live, who is there, what you do, what time you get up.
questions.hint: Don't write “financially free, traveling the world”. Write an ordinary Tuesday.
probes: What in that day do you already have?
What would you give up for that day?

questions.title: How long you're remembered
questions.prompt: By whom, and for how long, do you want to be remembered? If in the end no one remembers you, was being alive still worth something?
questions.hint: Write what you actually feel.
probes: Are you afraid of being forgotten?
What proves you were here?

questions.title: To yourself at 20
questions.prompt: If you wrote three lines to yourself at 20 right now, what would they say?
questions.hint: Write what you actually mean, not what's correct.
probes: Would you at 20 have listened?
Which line do you most need to hear now?

en.title: Language samples
en.subtitle: The chapter that decides whether it sounds like you
en.why: A lot of digital twins get things right and still don't sound like you. The difference is language: how long your sentences run, your punctuation, your catchphrases, when you use an emoji, how you swear, how you comfort someone. For this chapter, stay as close to the original as you can. Don't polish.

questions.title: Three real messages
questions.prompt: Paste three messages you actually sent: one to a friend, one to someone at work, one to family. (You can scrub names, but keep the tone and punctuation.)
questions.hint: Copy from your chat history. Don't rewrite. Keep the length, the typos, the emoji.
probes: What is the biggest difference in how you talk to the three?
Do you send voice messages?

questions.title: Something you wrote
questions.prompt: Paste something you wrote: a diary entry, a social post, an email, an article, a note to yourself.
questions.hint: Pick one you're satisfied with, or one that most represents you.
probes: How many passes do you make when you write?
Are you the same on the page as out loud?

questions.title: Your voice
questions.prompt: How you talk: pace, volume, accent, pauses, the words you lean on, the sound of your laugh. If it's easy, record a 60-second introduction, put it in the project, and write down the file name.
questions.hint: Recording is optional. Write an “I talk like…” comparison.
probes: Does your voice change when you're nervous?
Can people hear your mood?

questions.title: Four situations, exact words
questions.prompt: What do you say when you're angry, when you're comforting someone, when you're being soft or asking for something, when you're turning someone down? Write the actual words.
questions.hint: One or two lines for each. Imagine you're saying it to that person.
probes: Which line sounds least like you?
Do you have a go-to reply for everything?

questions.title: Emoji and punctuation
questions.prompt: Which emoji or stickers do you use? What are your three most-used ones? What punctuation do you type with?
questions.hint: A screenshot or a description, either is fine.
probes: Do you use periods?
Are your emoji politeness or actual feeling?

questions.title: The way you hate to be spoken to
questions.prompt: What way of talking do you hate? (Tone, word choice, the singsong, the sentence pattern.) Give examples.
questions.hint: Write the phrasing that irritates you the moment you hear it.
probes: Do you talk like that yourself?
What do you most hate being called?

en.title: Final check
en.subtitle: Write your own user manual
en.why: The last questions aren't memory. They're calibration. By writing down what counts as like me and what it must never say, you give the twin its edges. This chapter also becomes the grading standard for the check.

questions.title: Your user manual
questions.prompt: How should people deal with you? What kind of apology will you accept? How should someone turn you down without hurting you? When you need space, what should people do?
questions.hint: Like writing a manual for a new coworker, or a partner.
probes: What is the kind of care you hate most?
When you're hurting, do you want people to do something, or nothing at all?

questions.title: Where you're most misunderstood
questions.prompt: What do people most often get wrong about you? Why?
questions.hint: Write the point you've explained a hundred times and no one gets.
probes: How do you want to be understood?
Would you change in order not to be misunderstood?

questions.title: Shutting down, blowing up, running
questions.prompt: What makes you shut down, blow up, or want to run, instantly? Give one specific trigger for each.
questions.hint: Write the body signal and your first reaction.
probes: How long does it take you to come back?
Does anyone know how to bring you back?

questions.title: The last opinion you changed
questions.prompt: What did you last change your mind about? What changed it?
questions.hint: Big or small.
probes: Do you change your mind easily?
What would you never change?

questions.title: If only three lines survived
questions.prompt: If the digital twin could keep only three of your lines, which three?
questions.hint: A catchphrase, a creed, something you say to people often.
probes: Why those three?
Do those three represent you?

questions.title: What the twin must never do
questions.prompt: What should the digital twin never say or do? (Tone, content, promises, what it calls people, how it gives advice)
questions.hint: Write the red lines. For example: don't call me dear, don't agree to anything on my behalf, don't hand out platitudes.
probes: If it crosses a line, how should it repair it?
What topics should it avoid outright?

questions.title: How to tell it's like you
questions.prompt: How do you decide an answer sounds like you? Give three criteria, most important first.
questions.hint: For example: uses my words, doesn't over-explain, gives the conclusion first, admits it doesn't know.
probes: Which criterion matters most?
Which kind of “like me” is actually a stereotype?

questions.title: If it understood you better than you do
questions.prompt: If one day the digital twin understood you better than you do, would you be scared or glad? Why?
questions.hint: Write what you actually feel.
probes: What decisions do you want it to make for you?
What decisions must it never make for you?

ja.title: 座標と現在
ja.subtitle: まず今ここに戻す
ja.why: デジタルツインがいちばん陥りやすい失敗は、意見だけあって生活がないことです。この章ではまず、体、時間、お金、日常を入れます。それが、話すときの落ち着きと、疲れの出どころを決めているからです。

questions.title: 三つの文で自己紹介
questions.prompt: 今の自分を三つの文で紹介してください。一つ目は、自分は誰か（立場、役割）。二つ目は、今何をしているか（仕事、生活の重心）。三つ目は、今いちばん気にかかっていて、手放せないもの。
questions.hint: 履歴書のように書く必要はありません。真夜中に自分へ言う言葉として書いてください。三つで足ります。広げなくてかまいません。
probes: 一つだけ残せるなら、どれですか。
この三つのうち、いちばん自分らしくないのはどれですか。

questions.title: 基本の座標
questions.prompt: 生まれた年と場所、今どこに住んでいるか、誰と住んでいるか、何の仕事をしているか、母語・方言・外国語、家族の構成（親、きょうだい、婚姻、子ども）。
questions.hint: 自分だけが見るカルテを埋めるように、事実のリストでかまいません。
probes: この10年で何回引っ越しましたか。どの引っ越しがいちばん名残惜しかったですか。
今住んでいるところで、いちばん自分に似ている一角はどこですか。

questions.title: ふつうの平日
questions.prompt: 目を覚ましてから眠るまで、ふつうの平日はどう過ごしますか。時間の順に書いてください。起床、スマホ、食事、通勤、仕事、ひとりの時間、寝る前。
questions.hint: 細かいほどいいです。やるべきことではなく、実際にやっていることを書いてください。
probes: どの時間がいちばん自分らしいですか。
どの時間にいちばん逃げたくなりますか。

questions.title: ふつうの週末
questions.prompt: 予定のない週末は、どう過ごしますか。誰と、どこで、何をしますか。週末が予定で埋まっていると、どんな気持ちになりますか。
questions.hint: 理想の週末ではなく、直近の実際の週末を書いてください。
probes: ひとりの時間と人と会う時間の割合は、だいたいどれくらいですか。
週末が終わるとき、たいていどんな気持ちですか。

questions.title: 体という機械
questions.prompt: 今の体の状態です。睡眠、体力、運動、痛みや持病、食事、健康診断の異常の有無。体との関係はどうですか。
